newsitem.title: USA: LTV board OKs $66.6 mln steel investment.
newsitem.headline: LTV board OKs $66.6 mln steel investment.

text.p: LTV Corp said on Monday that its directors approved an investment of $66.6 million to improve the productivity, quality, cost and environmental performance of its steel making and sheet finishing operation.
About $60 million will be invested at the Cleveland Works, with the remainder being invested at facilities in East Chicago, Ind., the company said.

It said the investments will enable LTV Steel to increase the output capability of its existing cold rolling facilities by about 10 percent to satisfy the demand for its cold rolled, galvanized and pre-painted steel products.
About $10 million will be invested in rehabilitation and improvements to an air emission control system at Cleveland's Direct Hot Charge Complex steelmaking operation.
LTV said the improvements to the Cleveland Works finishing department will enhance the value of its product mix.

About one-half of LTV's cold rolled production is sold to the auto, appliance and electrical equipment markets for applications requiring a high-quality surface finish. The remainder of the cold rolled steel is processed into higher-value coated products, including hot dipped and electrolytically galvanized and prepainted steel.

The Cleveland Works flat rolled finishing improvements will consist of enhancements to Cleveland's existing 84-inch pickle line and 84-inch tandem mill and installation of a new steel slitting and inspection line.

LTV Steel also will upgrade the coil handling system at Cleveland's 84-inch hot strip mill to increase efficiency and reduce the potential for damage to the coils during handling. Installation of the previously announced $20 million "push-pull" pickle line continues with operation beginning in the second quarter of 1997.
Investments totaling $6.4 million will be made to increase the productivity and quality of the pickle line at LTV Steel's Indiana Harbor Works in East Chicago, Indiana.
